title: [CommandNotFound] Update winget module minimum dependency version

proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The missing minimum check is in the unchanged fresh-install branch, and its result is consumed by the Settings view model.
proposed_comments.title: Check the minimum WinGet Client version after a fresh install
proposed_comments.body:
### Check the minimum WinGet Client version after a fresh install
**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `InstallWinGetClientModule.ps1` after `Install-Module`, and `CmdNotFoundViewModel.InstallWinGetClientModule`.

**Problem:** The fresh-install branch reports `WinGet Client module detected.` when any version is discoverable. With a mocked initially empty inventory that returns `1.29.379` after installation, the current script emits that success message. Settings then marks the module detected even though it fails this PR's `1.29.380` requirement.

**Why it matters:** Settings can mark an unsupported dependency usable after installation, while the subsequent requirements check rejects it.

**Suggested change:**
1. Apply the same typed minimum-version check to the post-install and post-update inventories.
2. Report an outdated result when modules exist but none meets the minimum, and an absent result when no module is found.
3. Emit a single stable status for Settings to consume, separate from user-facing text, so both paths interpret the outcomes consistently.

**Verification:** Mock the initial empty inventory, then return no module, only `1.29.379`, `1.29.380`, and a mix of old and supported versions. Assert both the script status and the Settings detected state; only the last two cases should report a usable module.

confidence.rationale: A mocked run of the exact PR script reproduced the post-install false success, and the pinned Settings consumer maps that message to detected. No live gallery installation was performed.
